facts.text: Read the command word first: 'Describe' wants points listed, while 'Explain' and 'Why' want reasons.
The 1857 War of Independence was fought between the British East India Company and Indian soldiers and civilians — both Muslims and Hindus. It ended Mughal rule.
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the MAO College at Aligarh in 1875 to give Muslims a modern education; it later became Aligarh Muslim University.
The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906.
The Lahore Resolution was passed on 23 March 1940 — that is why Pakistan Day is marked on 23 March.
The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was the one time the Muslim League and Congress worked together, and Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
Pakistan gained independence on 14 August 1947, with Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as its first Governor-General.
The Indus is Pakistan's longest river and the backbone of the Indus Basin Irrigation System — the largest continuous irrigation network in the world.
Tarbela Dam sits on the Indus and Mangla Dam on the Jhelum — both store water and generate hydro-electric power.
Wheat is Pakistan's main food (subsistence) crop, while cotton is its most important cash crop.
In a 14-mark 'Was ___ the most important reason?' question, always weigh other factors too and finish with a clear judgement.
In source questions, use BOTH the source and your own knowledge — answers from the source alone rarely reach the top marks.
The first revelation of the Quran, 'Iqra' (Surah Al-Alaq), came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in the Cave of Hira.
The Hijrah — the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE — marks the start of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.
The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years: roughly 13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah.
